method.scenario: Synthetic direct Boss 2 with open reactor, collision protection and disclosed health floor; native game clocks. One production build/browser isolate, 60 s warmup and three 60 s observed windows. Normal UI Pause/Resume and countdown; debugger collection and exposeInternals snapshots only paused. One synthetic DOM blur after all windows.
method.retainers: Up to eight growing object/native classes, two new objects each, compared privately by snapshot IDs against warm baseline. Bounded shortest root paths exclude edges tagged weak. Constructor/native identifiers and approved property labels only. Not dominators, retained sizes, allocation stacks, complete native/GPU allocations or proof an object is unnecessary.
method.comparisonCoverage: All sanitized in-memory classes used before limiting exported differences, avoiding top-150 rank churn.

validation.wholeControllerExistingLint: Under the current local toolchain, both original baseline and candidate have 62 errors; warnings move 4 to 3. No controller-wide lint cleanup claimed.

findings.interpretation: Post-collection process memory rises by 27.023 MiB from warm baseline through cycle 3. The next snapshot lowers PSS again, emphasizing measurement timing/observer effects. No stable process plateau is established. Ordinary used heap rises by about 0.857 MiB. Snapshot code-type self sizes account for about 0.803 MiB of the 0.906 MiB total snapshot self-size increase; this is not a full process allocation attribution. Post-GC DOM/listener counts remain near baseline. Sampled growing network-resource objects have actual paths through the attached inspector. Other selected paths include browser performance-timing storage, live React/animation objects and generic events/current-context arrays; no blanket ownership attribution or unnecessary-object claim. These bounded examples do not explain the remaining process growth or native iPhone failure.
findings.pauseResult: All four normal UI pauses recorded manual-pause; the explicitly dispatched DOM blur recorded blur and entered paused without technicalPause. The synthetic blur still has focused=true and hidden=false, so it is not evidence of a real OS focus loss. Existing callback unit execution covers visibility-hidden, background-return and technical loop-stall separately.
findings.resourceCounters: One visible image, three canvases, reported sample audio buffers 6,925,568 bytes and measured hull/texture cache 422,836 bytes remain unchanged across paused comparison points. Browser decoder/GPU/native caches are outside this counter coverage.
